newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks stretch four-day rally.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks stretch four-day rally.

text.p: Argentine stocks soaked up mid-session profit-taking and closed higher for the fourth day running Friday, continuing their recovery from recent heavy losses, dealers said.
"The market continues to look good. It's aiming for the 900 mark, although it may first face some scattered profit-taking," said analyst Gustavo Grillo at brokers Roberto Agra y Cia.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV added 0.6 percent to end at 841.19, stretching losses since Tuesday to 6.2 percent. It rose 4.9 percent on the week.

"When the MerVal edged into negative territory today, cash flows fizzled. And blue chips kept a firm undertone throughout the day," Grillo said. "I think the market is already discounting the good company results we're likely to see when the corporate reporting season starts."

Floor volume eased to 36.8 million pesos from 45.8 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals shrank to 116.5 million pesos from Thursday's extremely heavy tally of 331.1 million which traders attributed to action by institutional investors.
"A lot of people took a break today, imitating the slower pace of business on Wall Street," another dealer said.
The broad market jumped 1.8 percent in the session, with winners outgunning losers 50 to 22 and 16 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia, which rallied 5.8 percent and 4.1 percent, respectively, and Telecom and Telefonica, up 4.1 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by foods giant Molinos, construction company Polledo and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which fell 3.9 percent, 2.9 percent and 1.6 percent, respectively.
